title: Prompt fragment pooling and locality-aware slab sharing
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Implement a cross-request prompt fragment pooling layer that reduces duplicate KV storage on GPU by co-locating identical prompt fragments into locality-aware slabs. The goal is to lower per-GPU memory footprint for multi-tenant workloads and improve effective KV cache hit rate for streaming/continuous-batching without increasing tail latency beyond the target SLOs. This ticket covers design, prototype, end-to-end benchmarks, and a staged rollout plan with telemetry and safety limits.
motivation: Observed workloads with high template reuse (system prompts, boilerplate instructions, SDK wrappers) store redundant KV entries per request. On high-concurrency instances this duplication leads to unnecessary GPU memory pressure and increases OOM risk, or forces smaller batch sizes. Pooling identical fragments and mapping them into shared slabs can reduce memory and enable larger batching windows for throughput improvements.
goals: Reduce duplicate KV storage by >= 40% on representative multi-tenant traces
Keep median and 95th percentile token generation latency increase <= 3ms on canary tests
Avoid cross-tenant data leakage: enforce tenant namespacing and access checks
Provide safe fallback to per-request KV when dedupe is disabled or if signature collision suspected
non_goals: Changing model weights or tokenization behavior
Replacing long-term snapshotting or persistent on-disk KV stores in this ticket
approach_summary: Build a lock-free read path: compute a short fingerprint for each prompt fragment (64-bit). Maintain per-GPU slab metadata that maps fingerprint -> slab pointer. Writes attempt to CAS-insert into an in-memory slab registry; collisions route to per-request allocation. Use a two-tier membership check (fast in-memory Bloom filter + compact fingerprint table) to reduce remote lookups. Background compaction merges small fragments into contiguous slab ranges and reclaims unreachable fragments during low load windows.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Fingerprint collisions: handled by conservative equality checks and per-fragment checksums; cost is occasional extra memory and degraded hit rate
Lookups add CPU overhead on the critical path; mitigate with vectorized hashing and caching of recent lookups
Eviction coordination across shards increases complexity; risk of transient double frees if not carefully ordered
Multi-tenant privacy: shared slabs must not expose content across tenants; we namespace registry entries but must validate memory isolation
design_decisions: Use 64-bit farmhash fingerprint for low-latency compute and acceptable collision profile
Keep slab metadata on-GPU to avoid device-host IPC on hot path; only metadata updates cross to host when necessary
Read path will be lock-free and wait-free where possible; write path may serialize on a thin host-side coordinator for slab allocation
Use Bloom filter with false-positive tuned to 1e-4 to avoid unnecessary metadata checks
No cross-tenant dedupe: registry entries are prefixed by tenant-id to guarantee isolation
implementation_plan: Spike: microbenchmark fingerprint cost and bloom-filter effectiveness (2 days)
Prototype: in-memory slab registry + lock-free read path on a single-GPU dev image (5 days)
Integration: wire into continuous-batching hot path; add per-request fallback and metrics (7 days)
Perf testing: run scaled replay of production traces and compare memory, latency, hit-rate (5 days)
Safety hardening: tenant namespacing, checksum verification, instrumentation, and runtime flags (3 days)
Canary rollout: enable for 10% of low-risk customers, monitor OOMs, latency, hit-rate, and errors (2 weeks)
Full rollout: expand after safety window and operator signoff
benchmarks_and_target_metrics: Target duplicate-KV reduction >= 40% on internal shared-template traces
Target overall token cost reduction >= 12% for mixed-generation workloads
Latency SLO: median token latency change <= +1ms, P95 <= +3ms
No increase in OOM frequency in canary cohort
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests covering read/write semantics and collision handling
Benchmark report comparing baseline vs pooled-slabs on replayed traces (attached)
Canary run shows no customer-visible regressions for 14 days and meets metric targets
Runbook updated with rollback steps and operator knobs to throttle dedupe
Security review signoff for tenant isolation checks
updates: 2026-02-11: Spike completed. fingerprint compute adds ~0.6us per fragment on x86; Bloom filter reduces metadata lookups by ~85% on sample trace.
2026-02-18: Prototype implemented in dev runtime. Lock-free read path working; write path uses host coordinator. Initial microbench shows 35% duplicate reduction on toy traces.
2026-02-24: Integration into continuous-batching pipeline done. Observed small P95 latency tail increase under synthetic fanout; investigating vectorized hash and caching improvements.
2026-03-03: Added checksum confirm step to avoid latent collision-based corruption. Slight memory increase for checksums but safer for correctness.
2026-03-10: Perf replay against 3 production slices: 42% duplicate reduction avg, token cost -9% overall. P95 increase ~2.3ms on one slice; optimizing hash pipeline.

2026-03-12: Ready for canary gating. Preparing rollout playbook and dashboard panels. PRs opened for runtime and metrics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1823 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/741
open_questions: What's the operational cost of periodic compaction at fleet scale? Need runbook limits and compaction concurrency tuning
Edge case: how to safely evict a slab referenced by a partially completed stream across devices?
Should we offer a tenant-level opt-out API or is platform-side control sufficient?
notes: Discussed with Product (Sofia Patel) — prioritized as P1 for next runtime release due to observed memory pressure on multi-tenant hosts
Design review feedback: prefer conservative defaults and feature flags to start; ensure strong telemetry around false-positive bloom hits
Coordination required with infra team for canary sizing and OOM alert routing
